summary: ETHIO-NASA is an offline-capable 3D satellite flight and spacecraft engineering game built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Space Mission Design Game prompt. Available as a lightweight (~4.5 MB) Android APK and local browser application, it lets players manage a $250,000,000 fictional career budget, design multi-stage spacecraft in a hangar, pilot ascents past 100 km into orbit, and align Earth-observation instruments over Ethiopian survey regions. It makes aerospace mission trade-offs and orbital mechanics accessible on everyday mobile devices without requiring an active internet connection.
details:
Play Live in Browser (No Install Required): https://ezrakidanu.github.io/ETHIO-NASA/

Connection to NASA Missions & Open Science:

ETHIO-NASA translates real engineering trade-offs used in NASA Earth-observing missions—such as Landsat and SWOT (Surface Water and Ocean Topography)—into interactive gameplay. Just as NASA mission architects balance launch vehicle payload capacity, solar array sizing, and delta-v budgets against mission cost, players must optimize hardware specifications before liftoff. Once in low Earth orbit, the 99.5% nadir-pointing alignment requirement teaches players how Attitude Determination and Control Systems (ADCS) and Reaction Control System (RCS) thrusters stabilize remote-sensing instruments over targeted geographic regions to capture valid Earth-observation telemetry.

What It Does & Gameplay Loop

ETHIO-NASA simulates the end-to-end engineering and flight lifecycle of a space mission from a fictional Ethiopian highland launch complex:

- Hangar & Budget Trade-Offs: Players start with $250,000,000 in fictional career funds. Before launching, they must select contracts and equip compatible bus structures, launch motors, power systems, and science instruments while balancing component prices, hardware specs, and launch-operation fees.

- Ascent & Orbital Insertion: Players pilot the launch vehicle using touch or keyboard attitude controls and main-engine throttle against simulated gravity and atmospheric drag. Reaching an altitude of 100 km unlocks the Deploy + Insert Orbit command, which separates the carrier rocket and spends a 6% propellant reserve to establish a circular orbit.

- Orbital Attitude Control & Science Capture: Once in orbit, players use Reaction Control System (RCS) thrusters and 3D attitude steering to point the satellite's underside science instrument toward a highlighted Ethiopian survey region, triggering data capture once sensor alignment reaches 99.5%.

Technical Architecture & Tools Used

- 3D Rendering & Simulation: Built with JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, and a locally bundled Three.js WebGL runtime (three.min.js) using a 1:50 display-world-to-metre scale and procedural 3D rocket, satellite, and terrain models.

- Offline-First & Mobile Packaging: Engineered with zero external network dependencies, persistent local career storage, and a standalone Android APK package (~4.5 MB) alongside full open-source browser files.
